sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: To express possession, Hungarian commonly uses a possessed noun with a dative possessor and van/vannak.

items.english: I have a friend in Budapest.

sections.content: Van becomes vannak the moment the possessed noun is plural — van egy barátom ('I have a friend') but vannak barátaim ('I have friends'). It's easy to forget this switch, because in English 'have' doesn't change at all for a plural object.
